data.narrative:
Floodbase is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bessie Schwarz and Dr. Beth Tellman. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 peers: 1 public company (Linanza, LNZA) and 8 private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach uses Floodbase's $17M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding an implied valuation of $34M. The Peer-Median method was not applicable: while 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, none satisfied the narrow filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comps), and a cross-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The single-method triangulation produces a range of $29M (low) to $39M (high), with a median of $34M. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of relying on stage-progression alone. Key limitations include the absence of sufficiently comparable peer data and dependence on assumed step-up multiples rather than direct market precedent. A future Series A follow-on or interim funding event would anchor valuation more reliably through actual comparable transaction data in the frontier-tech climate sector.
